technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot Test framework as the base testing infrastructure for U1 integration testing to leverage built-in test context management and Spring test utilities
Implement a pluggable in-memory mock message bus for U1 testing to eliminate dependencies on external message brokers (Redis, RabbitMQ etc.) during test execution
Use existing Spring Cloud YARN module deployment patterns as the baseline for the U2 YARNModuleDeployer strategy to ensure consistency with established Spring Cloud practices
Maintain full backward compatibility with existing Spring XD trigger module public APIs during U3 migration to avoid breaking changes for existing XD users
Extend the existing Spring Cloud Stream Redis binder implementation for U4 Redis Sentinel support rather than building a new binder from scratch to reduce effort and maintain consistency
Align U5 receptor-client upgrades strictly with the latest published Receptor API client contract specification to ensure compatibility with current Receptor server versions

Use Spring Boot's standard externalized configuration support (environment variables, system properties, application.yml) for U6 admin UI client server configuration to align with common Spring patterns

Follow Spring Boot auto-configuration conventions (including spring.factories registration and conditional bean creation annotations) for U7 singlenode binder auto-configuration to ensure ecosystem compatibility
Use Spring's Environment abstraction as the mechanism for U8 module access to injected YARN container definition parameters to ensure consistency with standard Spring configuration patterns
assumptions: All required third-party dependencies (Spring Boot, Spring Cloud Stream, Spring Cloud Data Flow, YARN client libraries, Receptor client, Redis Sentinel client, Hamcrest) are available and managed in the project's existing dependency management system (e.g., Spring Cloud BOM)

The existing s-c-s repository test infrastructure (test harnesses, CI pipelines, test environment provisioning) is fully functional and can be extended to support new testing requirements for U1, U4, U6, and U8
The Spring XD trigger module has no hard dependencies on Spring XD core components that cannot be replaced with equivalent s-c-s or Spring Boot components during U3 migration

The latest Receptor API changes are limited to minor version updates with no unannounced breaking changes to core client functionality beyond what is documented in the official Receptor changelog (U5)

The existing Spring Cloud Data Flow admin UI client supports configuration via standard Spring Boot externalized configuration mechanisms without requiring custom client-side UI build process modifications (U6)
Access to a test YARN cluster (or local YARN simulation environment) is available for development and testing of U2 YARNModuleDeployer and U8 YARN container parameter injection features
Access to a test Redis Sentinel cluster (or Testcontainers-based Sentinel environment) is available for development and testing of U4 Redis Sentinel binder functionality
All user stories are independent and can be developed in parallel with no cross-story blocking dependencies, allowing effort estimates to be summed directly without adjustment for parallelization
